records.region: Western Buenos Aires, Argentina: shallow lagoons, marshes and cultivated ground, ending in an eastern multi-pool wetland.
records.material_pending_reason: Permitted readable geographic evidence distinguishing the late-part 4 northeast return and part 5–7 central progression as one receiving lowland connection rather than a sequence of separate dune/interfluve-divided wet compartments. The exact whole-system representative name remains unsupported until this link and naming scope can be established.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No representative natural-river or receiving-system hydronym is supported for this exact selection. Regional Salado and canal names are not selected-route names.
records.completion_scope: The 110.005 km selected route crosses shallow lagoons, marshes and agricultural ground in western Buenos Aires and ends in an eastern multi-pool wetland. All 17 stored parts were visually reviewed. One central inter-depression transfer remains unestablished, so no representative river name is accepted and the finding remains source-material pending. Regional Salado/canal names are not substituted for this selection.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative natural-river or receiving-system hydronym is supported for this exact selection. Regional Salado and canal names are not selected-route names.

scope_limits: A continuous central inter-depression transfer across late part 4 and parts 5–7 is not established. The source shows surface cover but lacks the topographic discrimination needed to distinguish a common receiving floor from separate shallow compartments.
The finding does not demand exact banks, permanent water, a currently wet line, culvert verification or proof of contemporary canal operation.

Successful photographic terrain coverage is not silently promoted to complete hydrological correspondence. Conversely, ordinary dry or vegetated sections within an evident common wetland floor are not treated as separate gaps.
The eastern terminal wetland is geographically supported, but its local hydronym and present overflow destination are not identified.
The fixed model's endorheic terminal class and first/last positions are retained as attributes, without geometry correction or independent revalidation.

records.region: Baffin Island; inland waters northwest of the Nettilling Fiord coastal setting
records.material_pending_reason: The chosen small northern opening water and intervening lakelets have not been securely connected, at ordinary geographic scale, to the southern receiving lake/channel corridor that turns west. The imagery depicts several neighboring lakelets, elongated waters and bedrock-separated branches, but it does not sufficiently resolve which ordinary transfer carries the selected headward sequence into the researched downstream corridor. A connecting feature is not asserted absent. The gap is not a demand for exact vertex or bank alignment, an uninterrupted currently wet line, a surveyed source point or present hydraulic measurements.
records.geographic_disambiguation: No representative natural-river name is established. Nettilling Fiord is bounded coastal context from ARC402, and nearby McKeand River is excluded. The complete headward lake-chain transfer remains unestablished, while the lower connected open-water basins and separate source/render endings are geographically covered.
records.completion_scope: Bounded research pass concluded. The one selected stage3 mainstem, all33 stored parts and both ending descriptions were considered. A specific northern lake-chain transfer remains unestablished, so this is not a completed null name-scope hold. Clear downstream waterbody and outlet observations are retained without attaching a river name to the composite.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative natural-river name is established. Nettilling Fiord is bounded coastal context from ARC402, and nearby McKeand River is excluded. The complete headward lake-chain transfer remains unestablished, while the lower connected open-water basins and separate source/render endings are geographically covered.

scope_limits: The ordinary headward transfer remains unestablished; no disconnected basin or absent stream is asserted.
No supported representative natural-river name was found in the permitted material. This is not proof that local names do not exist.
The precise freshwater, brackish and marine boundary among the large lower water passages is unestablished.
Generalized selected segments differ from photographed shores and channels; no geometry correction, revalidation or channel-centreline repair was performed.
No formal registry, exact bank, surveyed endpoint, contemporary flow rate, ice hydraulics or management-operation conclusion is made.
Scene dates and seasonal consistency of the imagery mosaic were not independently established.

records.region: Northwest Territories, Smoke River corridor and southern Liverpool Bay coastal plain
records.candidate_name_role: Representative receiving-river system name supported by directly read cartographic labels and the connected selected corridor.
records.geographic_disambiguation: Smoke River represents the selected eastern lake-and-stream opening, westward upper corridor, northward middle river and westward coastal river. It does not separately rename each headwater waterbody, neighboring tributary, intertidal passage or the short rendered marine extension.
records.completion_scope: Directly read Stanton 107D NLUIS cartography supports Smoke River as the representative name. Its blue hydrography covers all 23 stored parts: the chosen eastern lake-and-stream opening, the westward upper valley, the broad northward turn and middle meanders, the westward coastal continuation, and the distinct source-mouth and rendered marine-terminal settings on the southern Liverpool Bay side. The complete ordinary geographic correspondence is supported without assigning the river name to every component or claiming formal registry verification.
records.supported_name_scope: Smoke River represents the selected eastern lake-and-stream opening, westward upper corridor, northward middle river and westward coastal river. It does not separately rename each headwater waterbody, neighboring tributary, intertidal passage or the short rendered marine extension.

scope_limits: Formal registry verification is unperformed, and no Korean name or application-ready scalar name is asserted.
The representative Smoke River candidate does not establish separate hydronyms for every small headwater waterbody or side channel.
The pinned model length is retained as inventory context, not represented as a surveyed Smoke River length.
Historical cartography supports ordinary geographic correspondence, not exact present-day shoreline, channel-bank position, current flow or tidal conditions.
The source-mouth and rendered sea-ending positions are distinct; their geographic settings are both accounted for without a geometry correction.

records.naming_scope_hold_reason: No representative natural-river name is supported for this complete selected composite. The sources identify several separate contributing or neighboring waterways; none is a demonstrated name for the entire receiving system.

records.completion_scope: Completed ordinary geographic correspondence for all33 selected parts, including the dry cultivated alluvial ending. Retained a completed null name-scope hold: the maps name separate tributaries and neighboring drainage, but do not support a representative natural-river identity for this selected composite.
records.supported_name_scope: No representative natural-river name is supported for this complete selected composite. The sources identify several separate contributing or neighboring waterways; none is a demonstrated name for the entire receiving system.

scope_limits: No direct main receiving-system hydronym was observed. Municipal waterway lists alone cannot assign one of their names to this composite.

Reference maps are generalized municipal thematic compilations. Geographic correspondence is at ordinary valley, fan and receiving-plain scale; it does not assert exact bank alignment or a surveyed name-transition point.

The photographic mosaic date was not independently established. Neither present flow nor year-round surface continuity, canal operation, drainage capacity or present land-management operation is inferred.
A continuous ordinary receiving floor is sufficient across dry, diffuse and cultivated passages; no blue line or currently wet thread through every patch is claimed.
The actual model ending has been inspected but is not demonstrated to be a named lake or a discrete natural hydrologic terminus. Source and render terminal descriptions remain separate.
The reconstructed historical restriction record is incomplete. Unlisted or omitted source identities are not implicitly cleared by this finding.

reconstruction_rule: Start from the pinned r46 cumulative index and apply later append-only deltas in verified commit order, rejecting duplicate IDs. publication_boundary: Own factual name/scope findings, public official URLs, bounded geometry metadata and public continuity pins only. No original maps, crops, complete coordinates or private source/derivative/registration fingerprints. Official hosting does not establish source redistribution rights.

research_order.progress_rule: Follow the actual continental order: Americas, Asia, Africa, Europe, then other, with all rivers before lakes. Preserve original queue IDs and ranks for continuity; apply documented geographic deferrals without counting them as name research, and place deferred objects into their corrected later phase by length-descending, stable-ID order. Prior candidate and scope-held assessments remain unresolved where stated.
